explainBack.question: What is the skin barrier, what are the five skin types, and how can you tell which type you have?
rubric: The skin barrier is the outermost layer of skin (stratum corneum), made of dead cells plus lipids such as ceramides; it keeps water in and irritants and bacteria out
Harsh products, over-exfoliating, hot water and skipping moisturizer can damage the barrier, showing up as dryness, flaking, stinging or rough patches

Dermatologists describe five types: normal (clear, not sensitive), dry (flaky, itchy or rough), oily (shiny and greasy), combination (dry in some areas, oily in others) and sensitive (stings or burns after product use)
You can identify your type by noticing how your skin looks and feels after cleansing (optionally pressing blotting paper on the T-zone and cheeks to check oil)
Products should be chosen for your skin type; sensitive skin generally does better with fragrance-free or hypoallergenic products

explainBack.question: How should someone wash and condition their hair, protect it from damage, and deal with dandruff?
rubric: Washing frequency depends on hair type: oily, straight hair may need daily washing, while dry, coarse or curly hair can go much longer between washes
Concentrate shampoo on the scalp rather than the full length, and use conditioner after shampooing (ends only for fine hair, full length for dry or curly hair)
Limit heat styling and use the lowest heat setting; wrap hair in a towel instead of rubbing, and avoid tight ponytails or buns that pull
Anti-dandruff shampoos contain ingredients such as zinc pyrithione, salicylic acid, selenium sulfide, ketoconazole or coal tar, and some should be left on the scalp for about 5 minutes before rinsing
Dandruff is not caused by poor hygiene; if it hasn't improved after about 4 weeks of anti-dandruff shampoo, or the scalp is red or swollen, see a doctor or dermatologist

explainBack.question: What does a complete daily oral hygiene routine look like, and what helps prevent bad breath?
rubric: Brush twice a day for about 2 minutes with a soft-bristled brush held at a 45-degree angle to the gums, using short strokes
Use fluoride toothpaste (NHS: at least 1,350 ppm for adults) and spit out rather than rinsing straight after brushing so the fluoride stays on teeth
Clean between teeth once a day with floss or interdental brushes
Replace the toothbrush every 3 to 4 months, or sooner if bristles are frayed
For fresher breath, clean the tongue daily as well; see a dentist if bad breath persists or gums bleed, and have check-ups at intervals the dentist sets (3 months to 2 years)

explainBack.question: Walk through how to shave to minimise irritation, and explain how to reduce razor bumps and ingrown hairs.
rubric: Soften hair first by wetting skin (e.g. after a shower or with a warm, damp cloth) and apply shaving cream or gel
Shave in the direction the hair grows and rinse the blade after each stroke
Replace disposable razors or blades after about 5 to 7 shaves and let the razor dry completely, stored in a dry place
Razor bumps/ingrown hairs happen when cut hairs curve back into the skin; they are more common with coarse or curly hair
Avoid pulling the skin taut or shaving too closely, and don't pick at bumps; see a dermatologist if bumps persist or become infected (persistent bumps can scar)

explainBack.question: What are the key habits for body hygiene, nail care and handwashing, and how do deodorant and antiperspirant differ?
rubric: Keep baths and showers to about 5 to 10 minutes in warm (not hot) water with a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser, then pat dry and moisturize within minutes
Antiperspirants use aluminum salts to reduce sweating; deodorants don't stop sweat but reduce odor by targeting odor-causing bacteria and masking smell
Cut nails straight across and round the tips slightly; don't bite nails or remove cuticles, and keep nails clean and dry
Wash hands with soap and clean running water, scrubbing for at least 20 seconds, then rinse and dry with a clean towel
If soap and water aren't available, use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol

explainBack.question: How can you tell whether a tailored jacket fits, and how do you read a care label and wash clothes so they last?
rubric: A jacket's shoulder seam should end where the arm meets the shoulder, and about half an inch of shirt cuff should show past the jacket sleeve
Care labels use five basic symbols: wash tub (washing), triangle (bleaching), square (drying), iron (ironing) and circle (professional cleaning)
In the symbol system, dots or numbers indicate temperature, bars under the symbol mean a gentler process, and a cross over a symbol means do not do it
In the US, care labels must give at least one safe cleaning method and warn against procedures that would harm the garment
Sort laundry by color (whites, lights, darks) and soil level, treat stains promptly, and don't overload the machine

explainBack.question: What causes acne, what do the common over-the-counter actives do, how should you test a new product, and when should you see a dermatologist?
rubric: Acne develops when hair follicles become blocked with oil and dead skin cells, and bacteria can then cause inflammation
Benzoyl peroxide targets acne bacteria, retinoids such as adapalene unclog pores, and salicylic acid helps unclog pores; give a treatment at least 4 to 6 weeks, as clearing can take 2 to 3 months
Use non-comedogenic products, avoid scrubbing, and don't pick or pop spots
To patch test, apply the product to a small spot such as the inner arm or bend of the elbow twice daily for 7 to 10 days, and stop if a reaction develops
See a dermatologist or doctor for nodules or cysts, acne that doesn't respond to over-the-counter treatment, signs of scarring, or acne affecting mental health
